title: The Lion and the Bull

full_text:
A crafty lion longed to feast upon the meat of a colossal prize bull, but the bull's massive horns, thick shoulders, and alert demeanor were so formidable that the predator dared not attack him in open combat.

Resolving to achieve by deceit what force could not accomplish, the lion approached the bull with a smooth smile and a bow of deep respect. "My esteemed friend," purred the lion, "I have slaughtered a fat, tender sheep in my den and have prepared a magnificent feast to celebrate our friendship. I invite you to dine with me as my guest of honor!"

The bull, flattered by the royal invitation, accompanied the lion to his rocky cavern. But as he crossed the threshold and peered into the kitchen, the bull noticed an enormous bronze cauldron bubbling over a roaring fire, surrounded by colossal butcher's spits and heavy cleavers large enough to carve an ox, but not a single trace of a sheep!

Without uttering a word, the bull turned abruptly and strode away down the mountain path at a rapid pace.

The lion ran after him, crying: "Why do you leave so rudely, friend Bull? Have I offended you? The feast is about to begin!"

The bull turned his mighty horns toward the predator and answered: "I have good reason to depart! A host who prepares a colossal cauldron and ox-sized spits has not slaughtered a little sheep for dinner; he has prepared the pot for the guest he invited!"
moral: False hospitality from a known predator conceals a deadly snare; look before you feast.
